what_it_does: This paper presents a millimeter-wave imaging chip that takes pictures of objects using radio waves in the 200 GHz frequency range, useful for scanning inside the body without radiation (biomedical imaging). The main challenge: building a dense sensor with 200 pixels while keeping each pixel small and sensitive. The authors use four techniques: (1) they boost the electrical Q-factor (energy concentration) of tiny resonators using active circuits so pixels can be packed tightly and each individually selected; (2) they share a single transmitter and receiver across all pixels instead of building per-pixel hardware; (3) they measure phase (timing shift) instead of raw power to avoid noise from free-running oscillators; and (4) they use a noise-canceling sampling method to suppress low-frequency drift. Together, these innovations enable a compact, sensitive, high-resolution imaging sensor.
